question: What is MediShield Life?
warm_answer: Great question — MediShield Life is a basic health insurance scheme that helps pay large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments, so a big medical bill doesn't fall entirely on you and your family.
warm_answer_alt: I'm glad you asked — think of MediShield Life as a basic health insurance scheme that cushions large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments, so a scary bill won't land on you alone.

question: Who does MediShield Life cover?
warm_answer: You're in good hands — MediShield Life covers all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, so nearly everyone here has this safety net for life.
warm_answer_alt: Here's the comforting part — every Singapore Citizen and Permanent Resident is covered by MediShield Life, so you and your loved ones are looked after.

question: Do I have to sign up for MediShield Life?
warm_answer: No paperwork to worry about — you do not need to apply for MediShield Life, as Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are covered automatically.
warm_answer_alt: No need to lift a finger — Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are enrolled in MediShield Life automatically, so you're covered without any application.

question: When did MediShield Life begin?
warm_answer: For a bit of history — MediShield Life started on 1 November 2015, giving everyone lifelong protection from that point on.
warm_answer_alt: A little reassuring background — MediShield Life has protected members ever since it started on 1 November 2015.

question: Does MediShield Life cover people who are already unwell?
warm_answer: Here's the reassuring part — MediShield Life provides lifelong coverage for everyone, including those with pre-existing conditions, so no one is turned away.
warm_answer_alt: This is the part people are relieved to hear — MediShield Life gives lifelong cover to everyone, including those with pre-existing conditions, so no one is left out.

question: From when are newborn babies covered?
warm_answer: Wonderful news for new parents — newborns who are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents are automatically covered under MediShield Life from birth, so your little one is protected right away.
warm_answer_alt: Such lovely news for your family — a Singaporean or PR newborn is automatically covered by MediShield Life from birth, protected from day one.

question: Which hospital ward class is MediShield Life meant for?
warm_answer: To set expectations kindly — MediShield Life is designed to cover subsidised treatment in Class B2 and C wards of public hospitals, which keeps everyday care affordable.
warm_answer_alt: Just so you know what to expect — MediShield Life is built around subsidised care in Class B2 and C wards of public hospitals, keeping essential treatment affordable.

question: What is the yearly claim limit of MediShield Life?
warm_answer: That's real peace of mind — MediShield Life covers up to $200,000 per policy year. For example, if a serious illness runs up $250,000 of claimable costs in one year, MediShield Life pays up to the $200,000 cap and the remaining $50,000 falls outside that year's limit; the next policy year the cap resets, so a $120,000 stay sits within it and is claimable in full (after the usual deductible and co-insurance).
warm_answer_alt: You're well protected — the yearly cap is $200,000. Say a patient's claimable bills reach $230,000 in Year 1: MediShield Life reimburses up to $200,000 that year, leaving $30,000 above the cap uncovered. In Year 2 a $90,000 bill sits comfortably under the reset $200,000 limit, so the whole bill is claimable (after deductible and co-insurance).

question: Is there a lifetime cap on MediShield Life claims?
warm_answer: You can rest easy — MediShield Life has no lifetime limit on the total amount you can claim, so long-term care stays supported.
warm_answer_alt: You can breathe easy — MediShield Life sets no lifetime limit on what you can claim, so long-term illness stays covered.

question: What is the daily ICU claim limit?
warm_answer: For the most serious moments — during an intensive care unit (ICU) stay, MediShield Life pays up to $5,140 per day, so intensive care is well supported.
warm_answer_alt: For the toughest days you're supported — MediShield Life covers up to $5,140 per day for an intensive care (ICU) stay.

question: How much is covered for kidney dialysis each month?
warm_answer: For ongoing treatment — MediShield Life covers kidney dialysis at up to $1,750 per month, easing the cost of regular sessions.
warm_answer_alt: For regular treatment this really helps — MediShield Life covers kidney dialysis up to $1,750 each month.

question: How much does MediShield Life cover for cancer drug treatment?
warm_answer: During a hard time this matters — cancer drug treatment is covered from $200 to $12,800 per month depending on the drug used, so treatment stays within reach.
warm_answer_alt: During a frightening time, cost worries ease — MediShield Life covers cancer drug treatment from $200 up to $12,800 a month depending on the drug.

question: How do I make a MediShield Life claim?
warm_answer: It's simpler than it sounds — just inform the medical institution that you want to claim from MediShield Life, and the hospital will submit the claim on your behalf.
warm_answer_alt: It's kindly kept simple — just tell the medical institution you want to claim from MediShield Life, and the hospital submits the claim for you.

question: Why is my private hospital bill reduced before claiming?
warm_answer: A gentle heads-up so there are no surprises — non-subsidised and private-hospital bills are pro-rated before MediShield Life works out the claim. For example, a $20,000 private-hospital bill is first scaled down to its subsidised-ward equivalent (say about $6,000) before the claim limits, deductible and co-insurance are applied — so the payout is based on the lower amount, not the full private bill.
warm_answer_alt: Good to know up front — because MediShield Life is pegged to subsidised (Class B2/C) rates, a private-hospital bill is pro-rated first. Imagine a $20,000 private stay: after pro-ration it might count as roughly $6,000 of claimable cost, and only then are the limits, deductible and co-insurance applied to compute the payout.

question: What determines my MediShield Life premium?
warm_answer: Helpful for planning ahead — your MediShield Life premium is based on your age and rises as you move into older age bands. For example, someone in the 21–30 band pays about $295 a year, while someone in the 66–70 band pays about $1,326 a year (before any subsidies).
warm_answer_alt: Good to budget for — premiums step up with each age band. A young adult (21–30) pays roughly $295 a year, whereas a senior in the 66–70 band pays around $1,326 a year before subsidies, since older ages carry higher expected claims.

question: How much is the MediShield Life deductible?
warm_answer: Here's what to expect — for a Class C ward stay the MediShield Life deductible is up to $2,000 per policy year, which you cover before payouts begin. For example, on $3,000 of claimable charges the $2,000 deductible leaves $1,000, and MediShield Life pays from there (minus a small co-insurance), so the deductible directly lowers the reimbursed sum.
warm_answer_alt: So you know what comes first — a Class C stay carries an annual deductible of up to $2,000. Picture a $3,000 claimable bill: subtract the $2,000 deductible and $1,000 remains for MediShield Life to work on — that is how the deductible reduces what you get reimbursed.

question: How often must I pay the deductible?
warm_answer: That's a relief for repeat visits — the deductible is payable only once per policy year, and it's waived for outpatient treatment. For example, if you're admitted in March and again in August the same year, the $2,000 deductible applies only to the first stay; the second admission has no deductible again, just co-insurance.
warm_answer_alt: Good news if you're admitted more than once — you pay the deductible only once a policy year. So a first hospital episode absorbs the $2,000 deductible, and a later episode that same year is computed without it (only co-insurance still applies).

question: What is the co-insurance under MediShield Life?
warm_answer: Your share stays small — after the deductible, co-insurance of between 3% and 10% of the claimable amount applies (smaller bills 10%, larger bills as low as 3%). For example, on the $1,000 left after the deductible, 10% co-insurance is $100, so MediShield Life pays $900 and you cover just the $100.
warm_answer_alt: Only a small slice is yours — once the deductible is taken out, you pay co-insurance of 3% to 10% of the rest. On a $1,000 claimable balance that's about $100 (10%), leaving MediShield Life to pay $900; the percentage shrinks toward 3% as the bill grows.

question: How can I pay my MediShield Life premiums?
warm_answer: Easy on your cash flow — MediShield Life premiums can be fully paid using your MediSave savings, so you usually don't pay out of pocket.
warm_answer_alt: Kind to your wallet — you can pay your MediShield Life premiums fully from your MediSave, so cash rarely leaves your pocket.

question: Can I pay my relatives' MediShield Life premiums?
warm_answer: Caring for loved ones counts — you may use your MediSave to pay MediShield Life premiums for family members such as your spouse, parents, children, siblings and grandparents.
warm_answer_alt: A nice way to care for family — your MediSave can cover MediShield Life premiums for loved ones like your spouse, parents, children, siblings and grandparents.

question: Is there an extra premium for pre-existing conditions?
warm_answer: Everyone stays covered, fairly — people with serious pre-existing conditions pay a 30% additional premium for the first 10 years, after which they pay the same as their age group.
warm_answer_alt: Handled fairly so everyone stays in — those with serious pre-existing conditions pay a 30% additional premium for the first 10 years, then the standard rate.

question: What is the highest premium subsidy available?
warm_answer: Help is there when needed — lower- to middle-income households can receive premium subsidies of up to 60%, keeping premiums affordable.
warm_answer_alt: Support is there when money's tight — lower- and middle-income households can get premium subsidies of up to 60%.

question: What income qualifies for premium subsidies?
warm_answer: To see if you qualify — premium subsidies are available to households with a monthly income of $3,600 or less per person.
warm_answer_alt: To check if this includes you — subsidies are offered to households earning $3,600 or less per person each month.

question: What premium help do Pioneer Generation seniors get?
warm_answer: Honouring our seniors — Pioneer Generation seniors receive premium subsidies of 40% to 60% plus yearly MediSave top-ups.
warm_answer_alt: Our Pioneer Generation is well looked after — they receive 40% to 60% premium subsidies plus yearly MediSave top-ups.

question: What subsidy do Merdeka Generation seniors receive?
warm_answer: A little extra for the Merdeka Generation — Merdeka Generation seniors receive an extra premium subsidy of 5%, rising to 10% after age 75.
warm_answer_alt: A thoughtful bonus for the Merdeka Generation — they get an extra 5% premium subsidy, rising to 10% once they turn 75.

question: What help exists if I still can't afford premiums?
warm_answer: No one is left behind — Additional Premium Support helps members who still cannot afford their premiums after subsidies and MediSave.
warm_answer_alt: No one is left struggling — Additional Premium Support steps in for members who still can't afford premiums after subsidies and MediSave.

question: What grant helps pay a newborn's premiums?
warm_answer: A lovely head start for babies — the MediSave Grant for Newborns is $5,000 and can fully cover a child's MediShield Life premiums until age 21.
warm_answer_alt: A warm welcome for new arrivals — the $5,000 MediSave Grant for Newborns can fully cover a child's MediShield Life premiums up to age 21.

question: What is the normal-ward daily limit for the first two days?
warm_answer: Here's how it helps in those first days — for the first two days in a normal ward, MediShield Life pays up to $1,630 per day. For example, a 2-day stay billed at $2,000/day is capped at $1,630/day, so $3,260 (not $4,000) is claimable before the deductible and co-insurance, which lowers the final payable amount.
warm_answer_alt: Good to know up front — your first two days in a normal ward are covered up to $1,630 each day. So if the ward charge is $2,000 a day, MediShield Life counts $1,630 a day; across two days that's $3,260 claimable, and the deductible and co-insurance then reduce the payable sum.

question: What does a normal ward pay per day from the third day?
warm_answer: And it keeps supporting you — from the third day onward in a normal ward, MediShield Life pays up to $830 per day. For example, in a 5-day stay the first two days are covered up to $1,630/day and days 3–5 up to $830/day, so those daily caps set how much of the bill is claimable before the $2,000 deductible and co-insurance apply, reducing the payable amount.
warm_answer_alt: For a longer stay you're still covered — from day three in a normal ward, MediShield Life pays up to $830 a day. In a 5-day stay that's $1,630/day for days 1–2 plus $830/day for days 3–5; those caps limit the claimable amount, and the deductible and co-insurance then determine the final payout.
